properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 10:57PM CDT until October 15 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southern Oklahoma, including the following
counties, Carter, Jefferson, Love and Murray and northern Texas,
including the following counties, Archer, Clay and Wichita.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms will continue
through Thursday morning. Storms will include very heavy rainfall
rates. Widespread additional rainfall amounts of 1-3 inches are
likely, and a few locations will see additional rainfall of up 5
inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 14 at 10:51PM CDT until October 15 at 1:45AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Glasscock County in western Texas...

* Until 145 AM CDT.

* At 1051 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Garden City and Saint Lawrence.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 14 at 8:23PM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 418 including Lake
Pillsbury, 419 including the City of Clearlake, Middletown,
Lower Lake, Indian Valley Reservoir, and other areas in
eastern and southern Lake County.

* WIND...Sustained winds of 20-25mph with gusts of 30-40mph
possible.

* HUMIDITY...Low overnight recoveries of 30-35% will drop to 15-
20% through the morning.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Hall; Childress; Motley; Cottle; Dickens; King; Kent; Stonewall
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 9:50PM CDT until October 15 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of the Rolling Plains and the Panhandle of Texas,
including the following counties, Childress, Cottle, Dickens, Hall,
Kent, King, Motley and Stonewall.

* WHEN...Through 12 PM on Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Significant amounts of rain have fallen over the past 24 hours,
with totals already exceeding 5 inches in spots. An additional
round of heavy showers and thunderstorms is expected overnight
through Thursday morning, which may result in additional flooding
and/or the continuation of flooding which is already ongoing.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
